content.value_statement: Azure AI Foundry project work often requires many SDK clients and resource types. This skill gives concise .NET examples for agents, connections, datasets, deployments, evaluations, indexes, and OpenAI clients.
actual_capabilities: Show package installation and authentication setup for Azure.AI.Projects.
Create, run, poll, read, and delete persistent agent workflows.
Create versioned agents with web search tools using Azure.AI.Projects.OpenAI.
Work with connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, and evaluations.
Show how to create Azure OpenAI chat clients from project connections.
List related SDK types, package names, and reference links.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources or manage subscriptions.
Examples require a valid Azure AI Foundry project endpoint and credentials.
Some APIs are marked preview and may change.
Does not include runnable project files or tests.

use_cases.title: Prototype Foundry Agents
use_cases.description: Create a persistent agent workflow with thread creation, run polling, message reading, and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Manage Project Assets
use_cases.description: Find examples for connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, and evaluations in one reference.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Choices
use_cases.description: Compare the high-level project client, persistent agents client, OpenAI extension, and related package names.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Project Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new .NET project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install the Azure AI Projects packages and create an AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a basic persistent agent flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a persistent agent that answers a user question, polls until the run finishes, reads messages, and deletes resources.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Project Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me a .NET plan for listing connections and deployments, uploading a dataset, creating an index, and running an evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Agent Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-ready Azure AI Foundry agent workflow using versioned agents, tool configuration, credential boundaries, async calls, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a persistent agent that solves a math question.
output: Agent, thread, message, run, polling, response reading, and cleanup steps.
Notes about async calls and resource deletion.

output_examples.input: Explain how to use datasets, indexes, and evaluations together.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines how to upload dataset files, create Azure AI Search indexes, run evaluations, and inspect evaluation status.

output_examples.input: Show a versioned agent with web search support.
output_examples.output: The response describes the preview package, agent definition, web search tool setup, response client use, and version cleanup.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential for production authentication and local development consistency.
Prefer async SDK methods for I/O operations and long-running agent workflows.
Request connection credentials only when needed and clean up created resources after experiments.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding project endpoints, connection names, or model deployment names in production code.
Leaving threads, agents, datasets, or indexes undeleted after experiments.
Using preview APIs without version checks or rollout controls.

faq.question: What SDK does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.AI.Projects for .NET and related Azure AI Foundry project workflows.

faq.question: Can it help create Azure AI Foundry agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes persistent agent and versioned agent examples with thread, run, response, and cleanup steps.

faq.question: Does it deploy Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains SDK usage and assumes the required Azure resources already exist.

faq.question: Does it include credential guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows DefaultAzureCredential and warns to request connection credentials only when needed.

faq.question: Are preview APIs included?
faq.answer: Yes. Versioned agents and some related packages are presented as preview features.

faq.answer: The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
